title: Tech Note: Analyzing the Request Log file
author: Jean-Yves Fock-Hoon
featured_technology: 4D Server request log file (SET DATABASE PARAMETER ID 28)
NEXT RECORD / GOTO SELECTED RECORD / GOTO RECORD performance comparison
Stored procedures, semaphores, GET PROCESS VARIABLE

historical_commentary.text: This note is a deep, request-by-request analysis of 4D Server's request log file, comparing the network cost of different ways to browse, modify, sort, and search a selection, plus stored procedure/semaphore and inter-process variable transfer patterns, all measured in raw bytes-in/bytes-out/duration per client-server round trip. It is a direct continuation of TN 06-03 and reflects a specifically Client/Server-era 4D architecture concern (minimizing chatty network requests over LAN/WAN) that remains conceptually important for performance tuning any client/server 4D application today, even though the exact request-log format and some cited command names are specific to this generation of 4D Server.
related_updates: 4D Server's request logging and client/server request-based architecture concepts described here have carried forward, though 4D has since added more modern diagnostic and monitoring tools (e.g., the SQL/ORDA-era network optimizations and newer Server Administration Window logs)
The specific request names and log format shown are tied to the mid-2000s 4D Server generation and may differ in exact naming in current 4D Server versions
